newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel lower against dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel lower against dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel's representative rate was fixed slightly lower against the dollar and the currency basket on Thursday in quiet trading, dealers said.
"After the representative rate was set on Wednesday the shekel started falling and the dollar rose above 3.4 shekels," said a dealer at Israel Discount Bank.

"On Thursday the shekel recovered a little when the dollar fell off highs against the mark and yen in Europe. The basket rose slightly amid demand from the business sector. The Bank of Israel wasn't seen in the market," he said.
The central bank has been intervening regularly in the market to defend the currency basket, which has been trading at the bottom end of its band for two months.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3930 shekels against 3.3900 on Wednesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6696 shekels against 3.6662 on Wednesday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 2.6971 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.6819 on Wednesday, and against the mark at 1.9780 shekels after 1.9758 on Wednesday.
In the late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.3940 shekels.
